amendments.rule: Where a Greek clause is verbless and the ASV supplies a copula, the copula is a rule 7 helper on the **predicate**, not on the subject. Where the predicate is a prepositional phrase the preposition takes it: `ἐγὼ ἐν τῷ πατρί` → *I am in the Father* gives *I* to the pronoun and *am in* to `ἐν`, as `ἐν ἐμοὶ ὁ πατήρ` → *the Father is in me*, `ὧν ἡ δόξα ἐν τῇ αἰσχύνῃ αὐτῶν` → *whose glory is in their shame*, and `ὧν τὰ ὀνόματα ἐν βίβλῳ ζωῆς` → *whose names are in the book of life* do. This is rules 31 and 32's copula clause holding outside a relative clause. Those rules give *are in* to `ἐν` and the copula to `μετά` where an article supplies the relativizer, and nothing in that reasoning depends on the article: a prepositional phrase has no verb to carry a supplied copula, so the preposition carries it whether or not an article stands in front. The same holds where the predicate is an adjective or an adverb, which likewise take the supplied copula themselves — `ὅμοια` → *were like*, `ἐγγύς` → *were nigh*. The recurring failure is reading the copula off the English word order and giving it to the subject pronoun, because the ASV writes *I am* together; word order is not what licenses a helper, and rule 27's warning points the other way here, since the predicate is what licenses the copula. This rule speaks only of a prepositional, adjectival or adverbial predicate. Where the predicate is a noun phrase, rules 7 and 17 decide it in the ordinary way, and there the subject pronoun is what takes the supplied copula: `ὑμεῖς τὰ κλήματα` → *ye are the branches* gives *ye are* to the pronoun, *the* to the article and *branches* to the noun, as `ἐγὼ τὸ Ἄλφα καὶ τὸ Ὦ` → *I am the Alpha and the Omega* does. What decides this is not the word order the rule has just refused, but what is left to carry the copula: a prepositional, adjectival or adverbial predicate is a source token whose own English is what the copula predicates, whereas a noun phrase spells its article and its noun out in words that already answer to those tokens and leaves nothing inside it for the copula, so the copula stays with the subject the ASV supplies its person and number from. A **verbless predication embedded under an expressed finite Greek verb** is such a clause, and the matrix verb's being expressed does not exempt it. Where the ASV renders a Greek object-complement or secondary-predicate construction by an English frame whose copula is written as an infinitival ***to be*** — *found … to be*, *shown to be* — that *to be* is the embedded predication's own supplied copula and is decided here rather than by rule 7 on the matrix frame: the embedded predicate carries it under this rule and rules 63 and 68, and the matrix verb keeps only the English word rendering its own lexeme. `εὑρέθη μοι ἡ ἐντολὴ … αὕτη εἰς θάνατον` → *this I found to be unto death* gives a bare *found* to `εὑρέθη`, a bare *this* to the demonstrative, and *to be unto* to `εἰς` headed on *unto*, exactly as the same verse's `ἡ εἰς ζωήν` → *which was unto life* gives *was unto* to its own `εἰς`; and `ἵνα φανῇ ἁμαρτία` → *that it might be shown to be sin* gives *it might be shown* to `φανῇ` and *to be sin* to the predicate noun under rule 68, that embedded clause expressing no subject of its own. The frame licenses the word but does not carry it, and the recurring failure is reading a *found … to be* or *shown to be* as one matrix idiom because English writes the two parts together. Rule 61 is not the contrast: its infinitival marker stands in front of a verb the Greek expresses, whereas here no source token answers to *be* at all. Rule 96 is untouched, the frame it keeps whole on a negator being an English cleft, which predicates nothing of a token of its own.
amendments.why: Rule 53's opening sentence reads as though a sentence carrying any expressed finite verb were outside it, and that reading cost ROM.7.10 an error: the verse folded the supplied *to be* of *found … to be* into εὑρέθη under rule 7 while giving the parallel supplied *was* of the same verse's other εἰς to the preposition, and while ROM.7.13 gave the identical supplied *to be* to its embedded predicate noun. The amendment states the scope the rule's own operative principle already implies — decide a supplied verb by what is left in the predication to carry it — and names the English infinitival copula as the shape that hides it, since rule 61's marker clause and rule 7's licensing test both pull the other way for a word spelled *to be*. It is returned as an amendment rather than a new rule because the over-broad sentence is inside rule 53 itself, and a cross-reference would leave it there for whoever reads it first. The evidence is two instances in this chapter, one of them self-contradicting within its own verse, plus the whole 53/62/63/68/96 chain, no arm of which puts a supplied verb on a matrix verb; the scoping clauses expressly leave rule 96's cleft frame and rule 61's marker where they stand, so nothing already settled is reopened.

conventions: The ASV writes a bare *sin* everywhere in this chapter, so every Greek article governing ἁμαρτία is `unrepresented` under rule 23 — 7:7, 7:8, 7:9, 7:11, 7:13 twice, 7:14, 7:17, 7:20, 7:23 — while every anarthrous νόμος takes the ASV's supplied *the* as its own rule 7/51 helper — 7:1, 7:7, 7:8, 7:9, 7:25 twice. The two patterns are the chapter's characteristic pairing and a reference comparison reports the empty articles as disagreements; that report is not a correction.

The parallel clefts of 7:17 and 7:20, οὐκέτι ἐγὼ κατεργάζομαι αὐτό → *it is no more I that do it*, keep the English cleft frame *it is* whole on οὐκέτι under rule 96's expressed-verb clause; ἐγώ takes a bare *I* as the cleft's focus and the verb keeps the relativizer *that*. Splitting *it is* off onto ἐγώ remains the competing reading, and both verses take the same one.

ROM.7.9/7.10 is a versification boundary under rule 37. The projection places ἐγὼ δὲ ἀπέθανον at the head of 7:10 and the ASV translates it at the end of 7:9 as *and I died*: that English is `added` in 7:9 and the three source tokens are `unrepresented` in 7:10, each side naming the other and neither reaching across.

report: One genuine cross-verse split: ROM.7.10 against ROM.7.13. Both embed a verbless Greek predication under an expressed finite verb (εὑρέθη, φανῇ) whose copula the ASV writes as an infinitival *to be*. ROM.7.13 gives *to be sin* to the predicate noun ἁμαρτία; ROM.7.10 folded *to be* into εὑρέθη as part of an English *found … to be* frame. Nothing in the source licenses the difference.

ROM.7.10 also contradicted itself: the same verse gives *was unto* to the first εἰς under rules 31 and 53 and only a bare *unto* to the second. Rule 53's chain (53, 62, 63, 68, 96) puts a supplied verb on the predicate in every arm and never on a matrix verb, so the reconciliation runs toward the predicate. Patched ROM.7.10 only: εἰς (s013) now takes *to be unto* headed on *unto*, and εὑρέθη keeps a bare *found*. ROM.7.13 was already right and is untouched.

Everything else in the 46-lemma table is the ASV rendering one word differently where the source licenses it. Checked in full: μέν empty at 7:12 and *indeed* at 7:25 (rule 70's English-side test); ὅ → *that which* headed on *which* at 7:15 against the substantival τό headed on *that* at 7:13 and 7:18, which is rule 77's own division and not a split; fourteen bare-*sin* articles against five anarthrous νόμος units taking a supplied *the*, which are rules 23 and 51 applied consistently; χωρίς keeping its trailing *from* at 7:8 and 7:9; καρποφορέω headed on *bring* at 7:4 and 7:5; the two μὴ γένοιτο and the two εἰ μή; the parallel clefts of 7:17 and 7:20; the articular-infinitive articles at 7:4, 7:5 and 7:18, which rule 61 covers on both the governed and the ungoverned arm.

The two `added` units, which the lemma table is blind to, are both sound: the supplied appositional *even* at 7:4 stands on rule 105's article-carrier arm, and *and I died* at 7:9 is the rule 37 versification boundary, matched by three `unrepresented` tokens at the head of 7:10 with a note naming the other verse on both sides.

BSB: none of the six disagreements is a genuine error. ROM.7.5 τό and ROM.7.18 τό are nominalizing articles of articular infinitives (rule 61); ROM.7.7 τε and ROM.7.12 μέν are rule 70; ROM.7.25 τῷ is an article the ASV gives no determiner (rule 23); ROM.7.21 ἐμοί is the doubled dative for which the ASV writes *to me* once, already carrying the competing reading in its own unit note. No accepted edge was touched to move that figure.

Two contested units left standing as the verse passes decided them, both with their notes intact: ROM.7.24's *that I am* on ἐγώ (rule 56, ταλαίπωρος being spent on *Wretched* outside the relative clause) and ROM.7.6's *to* folded into ἀποθανόντες. Neither recurs elsewhere in the chapter, so neither is a consistency question.
